result.title: Augmentation-Guided Adversarial Training via Local Stability-Based Sample Selection
result.summary: Adversarial training remains one of the most effective defenses against adversarial attacks, but its standard PGD-based training is computationally expensive because adversarial examples are generated for every training sample. Selective adversarial training reduces this cost by perturbing only a subset of samples. However, existing selective techniques typically rely on point-wise difficulty signals such as loss, entropy, margin, or gradients. We show that these point-wise criteria do not capture local instability in a sample's neighborhood. Motivated by this, we propose Augmentation-Guided Adversarial Training (AGAT), a selective adversarial training framework that uses augmentation-induced local variation to allocate samples with unstable neighborhoods for adversarial training. AGAT ranks samples using Augmentation-based Local Stability (ALS), a lightweight score that measures the normalized change in model logits between an input and its label-preserving augmented variant. Experiments across different architectures on MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet-200 demonstrate that AGAT achieves comparable or higher robust accuracy while applying adversarial supervision to only 20-30% of the training samples in each minibatch. AGAT also requires less training time than all other adversarial training baselines in the computational cost evaluation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 AGAT，用「增强诱导的局部稳定性」打分（输入与其保标签增强变体之间 logits 的归一化变化）来挑选每个 minibatch 中约 20–30% 的样本做对抗训练，在多个图像分类数据集上取得相当或更高的鲁棒精度并减少训练时间。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以邻域局部不稳定性替代 loss/entropy 等逐点信号来分配训练监督的做法，可能可供核查作为 LVR 中训练样本或推理轨迹筛选、监督贡献分配的线索；但论文只做图像分类鲁棒性，未涉及视觉-语言推理或 latent 状态本身。
